$comment: The canonical PostHog actions, tagged 'canonical' in the project. `mise analytics:check` fails when the live canonical actions differ from this file or when a catalog event's previous_names is not covered here; `python3 scripts/ci/analytics.py sync-actions --apply` makes the project match. A renamed event's old name carries a timestamp bound wherever the two names overlapped, so the union never double counts.

actions.name: Active user (human)
actions.description: SINGLE SOURCE for 'active user' across all dashboards — reference this action, never re-list events. A person is active on a day they used GAIA: sent a chat message (web, desktop, mobile, voice or a linked bot) or ran a workflow themselves. Signup, onboarding, page loads, paywall hits and settings changes are not use. The steps are the facts in shared.py.analytics.activity.ACTIVE_USE_EVENTS, which user:active is emitted from (a test keeps the two equal), so the series means the same before and after user:active was narrowed to them on 2026-11-03; renamed events carry the same bounds as their continuity actions.

actions.name: Chat message submitted (continuous)
actions.description: One accepted chat turn across the 2026-08-18 rename. chat:message_sent (web client) counts only before 2026-08-17 11:25:02.541 UTC, the first chat:message_submitted; the two overlapped on Aug 17-18, so an unbounded OR would double count those days. Before the cutover the series is web-only; after it, every surface.

actions.name: Workflow created (continuous)
actions.description: Workflows a user asked for. workflows:created (web client) before 2026-08-18 19:16:12.478 UTC, the first server-side workflow:* event, then workflow:created except, on events from before origin existed, is_todo_workflow true: the workflows generated unasked with every new todo (they also held the few a user requested from a todo, which cannot be told apart). Todos no longer generate workflows unasked. The web emitter stopped on 2026-08-16, so the bound only guards the cutover.

properties.key: NOT (properties.origin IS NULL AND properties.is_todo_workflow = true)

actions.name: Workflow executed (continuous)
actions.description: workflows:executed (web client) before 2026-08-18 19:16:12.478 UTC, the first server-side workflow:* event, then workflow:executed. The web emitter stopped on 2026-08-16, so the bound only guards the cutover.

actions.name: Workflow published (continuous)
actions.description: workflows:published (web client) before 2026-08-18 19:16:12.478 UTC, the first server-side workflow:* event, then workflow:published. The web emitter stopped on 2026-08-16, so the bound only guards the cutover.

actions.name: Workflow unpublished (continuous)
actions.description: workflows:unpublished (web client) before 2026-08-18 19:16:12.478 UTC, the first server-side workflow:* event, then workflow:unpublished. The web emitter stopped on 2026-08-16, so the bound only guards the cutover.

actions.name: Workflow deleted (continuous)
actions.description: workflows:deleted (web client) before 2026-08-18 19:16:12.478 UTC, the first server-side workflow:* event, then workflow:deleted. The web emitter stopped on 2026-08-16, so the bound only guards the cutover.

actions.name: Workflow steps regenerated (continuous)
actions.description: workflows:steps_regenerated (web client) before 2026-08-18 19:16:12.478 UTC, the first server-side workflow:* event, then workflow:steps_regenerated. The web emitter stopped on 2026-08-16, so the bound only guards the cutover.

actions.name: Notification read (continuous)
actions.description: notification:dismissed (web client) before 2026-09-17 13:42:36.633 UTC, the first server-side notification:read, then notification:read.

actions.name: Rate limit hit (continuous)
actions.description: rate_limit_hit, then rate_limit:hit after the event catalog rename. One server emitter changed its name in one deploy, so the two never fire for the same hit and need no date bound.

actions.name: Approval decided (continuous)
actions.description: approval:decided (the retired interrupt path; historical events only) or hil:decision_submitted (the approval ledger, the only path since the interrupt path was deleted).

actions.name: Instructions updated (continuous)
actions.description: integration:instructions_updated before the rename, then instructions:updated. The old name covered only per-integration instructions and was emitted by the code the rename replaced, so the two never overlap and neither is date-bounded; instructions:updated also counts global instructions (scope_kind=global) and GAIA's own saves (updated_by=agent).
